method: Read-only follow-up review of final portable, native, adapter, host, service, CLI and UI boundaries. The reviewer implemented the host/UI slice earlier in this round. This report is neither an independent penetration test nor an extra execution of real-engine or package acceptance.

resolvedFindings.before: Schema 2 with 128 distinct released rows per step returned runtime_control_limit at 9/10 steps but runtime_control_invalid at 11/64 steps because the unchanged 8192-node defensive copy budget ran first. This safely rejected execution but contradicted the agreed row-budget error code and service HTTP 422 status.
resolvedFindings.repair: The core owner added a descriptor-only bounded container count before copying. Accessors and malformed containers are never executed; the 8192-node defensive copy limit was not widened. Over-budget valid collection shapes now retain runtime_control_limit.
resolvedFindings.verification: Portable final 45/45 includes a new 9/10/11/64-step regression and getter/container defenses. The existing host/service admission test additionally checks 11/64 x 128 rows => runtime_control_limit / 422, unchanged owned job IDs and an invalid row getter with zero invocations. Final host/UI regressions with real Godot 4.7.2, Bevy native0.3.0 and native core enabled pass 69/69, with zero failures or skips; the new host/UI subset remains 12/12.

resolvedFindings.before: The root actual 390px browser screenshot showed closed-select labels truncated before the distinguishing UUID suffix. Same-name instances with the same UUID prefix were therefore indistinguishable in the selected display.
resolvedFindings.repair: Instance labels now put the last eight UUID characters before the bounded authored name, retaining the complete UUID and name in title and the original complete instance UUID as option value. No contracts or authored values changed.
resolvedFindings.verification: The existing same-definition target-choice semantic test verifies distinguishable leading identity, preserved name and full identity in title. UI replay/build/object regressions pass 42/42; the root owns the follow-up actual browser screenshot and prepared-resource checks.

boundaries.conclusion: Exact schemas 1/2, boolean rows, detached frozen values, finite fixed step/duration, full final release and schema-2 sparse steps remain bounded. Schema 2 counts at most 128 rows per step and 1024 across the program; the separate all-actor sample budget is actorCount x stepCount <=1024. Descriptor-only preflight preserves the actionable row-budget diagnostic without getter execution or relaxing deep-copy defenses.

Schema 2 requires runtime/plan2 and both global and instance replay capabilities. Only instance UUIDs declared in the revalidated frozen plan are admitted; repeated object definitions remain separate instances. A definition UUID is rejected unless it is also genuinely a declared instance UUID. Empty-input programs still cannot bypass plan-version admission.

Godot clears its instance input dictionary on every step; Bevy replaces its optional input map on every step. Missing rows produce zero direction in that step. Both preserve controls:none and zero-speed movement rules, opposing-direction cancellation and diagonal normalization. The host and portable layer do not implement movement or synthesize coordinates.

Public targets contain only instanceId, objectId and a bounded display name captured from a successful frozen build. Private admission uses minimal frozen plan identities. Status responses are detached; later author edits and response mutation do not alter cached targets. Target, duplicate, row-budget, capability, mode and foreign-build errors are rejected before creating/replacing the owned job slot. HTTP accepts only values and opaque service-owned identities, never file/tool/backend paths.

The host validates snapshot/source-restored plan, generated backend, execution fingerprint, exact local tool identity and generated artifact inventory before allocating a control session. Adapters stage bounded canonical programs and the trusted Godot wrapper under fixed exclusive session filenames, validate targets before spawning, and remove staged data in finally. The host removes its independent runtime project; authored documents/resources and frozen original output are untouched.

Schema 2 reuses trace schema1 and runtime protocol2. A single ordered reader checks ready, sequential complete all-actor samples, paired instance/object identity and a matching final frame. Samples do not shrink to just the input rows. Malformed frames remain errors; cancellation/failure retains last admitted samples. Separate observation/sample storage survives raw-event ring rotation and cannot be changed by progress consumers.

Only CLI reads the caller-selected control JSON regular file, bounded at 256 KiB with the existing schema1 16 KiB check preserved; only canonical values reach the host/adapters. Godot adapter0.5.0 and Bevy adapter/native0.3.0 both expose runtime.control-replay.instances, retain contract1 and the seven execution keys, and reject behavior plan3 replay. Schema1/global and ordinary smoke payloads retain their previous semantics.

boundaries.area: UI intent, target choice and draft preservation
boundaries.conclusion: The target selector offers instance choices only from the current owned plan2 build with both replay capabilities. A leading UUID suffix makes same-name instances distinguishable in a narrow closed selector; full UUIDs remain in option values and titles. Names/IDs render as text. Selection changes only local choice; explicit Generate input example replaces JSON. Polling, reopening and locale changes preserve local JSON and caret. Changed ownership clears stale selection without silently rewriting JSON. Live dirty/creating/busy/active-job guards prevent generation and replay; friendly invalid/foreign-target errors remain local, while ordinary headless requests omit controlProgram.

limitations: The configured native executable and installed Godot tool are trusted local host programs. Hash/version identity is neither signing nor protection against another process with the same user permissions.

This scope is finite global or per-instance direction replay on Scene2D plans1/2. It does not add real-time input, arbitrary actions/components, author Rust/GDS behavior replay, stdin/RPC/BRP, GPU execution or a rendered viewport.
The portable layer checks identities and frame shape, not the physical truth of engine movement. Coordinates are samples and can become stale after subsequent state frames.
Godot Vector2 and Bevy f64 precision differ. Representative coordinate evidence does not promise bitwise parity for arbitrary trajectories.
The 256 KiB CLI/native file limit is separate from semantic row/sample/duration and defensive pure-data budgets; a file under its byte limit is not automatically a valid program.

Real browser, engines, offline prepared resources, full application and mobile pure-module results are separate evidence owned by the root. This review did not rerun native Tauri or Android device execution.
Current documentation and atlas require a separate final review after their source freeze; this boundary report does not declare those documents final.
